name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 21 points
Overwhelming fundraising gap: Taylor $1.6M raised vs. about $1,000 for Mazzuckelli
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 1%
No public polling; fundamentals and incumbent advantage dominate
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, a well-funded incumbent seeking another term, and a Democratic challenger who has raised roughly a thousand dollars leave virtually no path to an upset, and markets agree at near-certain Republican odds.
model.watch: Only a major scandal involving Taylor or a sudden influx of outside spending for the challenger would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's second district, anchored in southwestern Ohio, leans heavily Republican, and incumbent David Taylor enters the general election holding the advantages that typically decide races here. The partisan baseline favors Republicans by roughly twenty points, and while the broader national environment offers Democrats some offset, it is nowhere near enough to close a gap of this size.

Taylor has raised about $1.6 million and reports more than $700,000 on hand, while Democrat Jennifer Mazzuckelli has reported roughly $1,000 raised and almost no cash, signaling a token challenge. No public polls track the contest, and prediction markets give Democrats about a one percent chance. Absent an unexpected development, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin.
